{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Desserts]]

'''French macarons''' are variety of [[Cookbook:Sandwich Cookie|sandwich cookie]] based on almond [[Cookbook:Meringue|meringue]] and a sweet filling.

== Ingredients ==
* 125 g [[Cookbook:Icing sugar|icing sugar]]
* 125 g [[Cookbook:Almond Flour|almond flour]]
* 125 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] white [[Cookbook:Superfine Sugar|superfine sugar]]
* 90 g (3 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]].) [[Cookbook:Egg White|egg whites]]
* [[Cookbook:Food Coloring|Food coloring]] (concentrated variety)
* Filling as desired (see notes)

== Preparation ==
# Combine the almond flour and icing sugar. Sift to remove lumps, and set aside.
# Add the superfine sugar to the egg whites, and [[Cookbook:Whipping|whip]] them to stiff peaks.
# Add the food coloring to the egg whites and continue beating until incorporated.
# Use a wooden spoon or rubber spatula to [[Cookbook:Fold|fold]] the almond flour mixture into the meringue in 3 batches. Mix until you get a lava-like batter (see notes). 
# Transfer the batter to a [[Cookbook:Pastry Bag|pastry bag]] fitted with an 8 mm round nozzle. Pipe 3 cm rounds on a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]] lined with [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|baking paper]].
# Tap the sheet lightly on your work surface to even and flatten the mixture. Leave to air-dry for 30 minutes until a film forms on the surface of the cookies.
# [[Cookbook:Bake|Bake]] for 12 minutes at 150°C with convection.
# Remove from the oven and let cool completely. It's a good idea to move the parchment onto a [[Cookbook:Cooling Rack|cooling rack]] to avoid carryover cooking.
# Peel the shells from the parchment, and sort them into pairs of equally sized shells.
# Sandwich the cookies together with your desired filling.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Common fillings for macarons include jam, buttercream frosting, and ganache.
* [[File:Delish macaron, June 2009.jpg|thumb|Under-mixed macaron—note the hollowness inside, uneven texture, and rounded top]]It's very important to get the batter to the correct texture when making macarons. After adding the almond mixture, the mixture will get thinner as you continue to fold it. If it is too thick, you won't get nice, smooth, even shells—they will be too stiff and full of air. On the other hand, if the batter gets too thin, it will spread too much and will not hold the proper cookie shape. Your goal is to stop folding the batter when it flows off the spatula in a ribbon (not in one clump) and takes about 10 seconds (not less) to dissolve back into the rest of the batter.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sally |date=2021-03-01 |title=Beginner's Guide to French Macarons |url=https://sallysbakingaddiction.com/french-macarons/ |access-date=2024-10-19 |website=Sally's Baking Addiction |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Mike |date=2020-05-15 |title=The Ultimate French Macaron Guide |url=https://mikebakesnyc.com/ultimate-french-macarons-guide/ |access-date=2024-10-19 |website=MikeBakesNYC |language=en-US}}</ref> Note that you cannot go back once you have over-mixed the batter.
